findings.title: Undrained bytes behind the header terminator reset the socket and truncate the body

findings.description: A decoded 0x20 in the proxy path passes the c<32 guard and produces a four-token upstream request line; a whitespace-splitting upstream executes the smuggled query.
findings.title: Space in the path defeats the `c<32` guard and splits the upstream request line

findings.description: query sliced from raw target (line 50) and appended undecoded at pt (line 50); path guard ch<32/127 never applies; %0d%0a in query splits upstream line and execs /exec?cmd=id (uid= returned); works URI and bare proxy_pass; path CRLF control still 400
findings.title: Query string is forwarded undecoded and unvalidated, so `%0d%0a` in the query splits the upstream request line where the path guard would reject it

findings.description: header erased at line 54 then 405 returned at line 50 with the body undrained; body stays in c.in and is parsed as the next request; one client write -> 3 responses, 2 upstream requests, body proxied to /exec?cmd=id (uid=); no control bytes needed
findings.title: A rejected POST leaves its body in the parse buffer, so the body is re-read as the next request and proxied

findings.description: upstream head split on CRLF at line 57 and relayed unfiltered; bare LF hides the next header inside a value; strict reader sees 0 CL / 1 TE, lenient sees CL+TE (or 1 vs 2 CL)
findings.title: Upstream headers carrying a bare LF are relayed verbatim, giving CRLF-strict and LF-lenient parsers different header sets and framing

findings.description: every interim response is turned into a 502 after the upstream has already answered
findings.title: Interim (1xx) upstream responses are rejected as parse failures, so any upstream that emits one returns 502

findings.description: the whole request is refused before the target is even parsed; the request is refused with 417
findings.title: `Expect: 100-continue` is refused outright with 417, so every standard uploading client is rejected

findings.description: The framing gate rejects any request carrying a `Transfer-Encoding` header, so chunked uploads (curl -T) never reach the upstream. the header test sits in the same clause that gates every non-`GET` method.
findings.title: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` request bodies are refused with 400, so every standard chunked upload fails

findings.description: A response carrying both framings is 502'd. the `chunk` flag and the parsed `length` are both kept, and their conjunction is fatal.
findings.title: A legal upstream `Transfer-Encoding` + `Content-Length` pair is rejected with 502

findings.description: SIGTERM signals workers, which close downstream sockets at once; an in-flight proxied response is cut at 0 bytes while the accepted drain deadline is never referenced.
findings.title: SIGTERM truncates the in-flight proxied response and the configured drain deadline is unused

findings.description: toksec_pipeline_depth is not in any directive list and setting() has no terminal else, so the name is accepted by --check-config and discarded; depth 1/4/64/unset all behave identically. The reader also decodes one request per poll pass after draining the whole batch, so every pipelined request waits the 100 ms poll timeout: 20 pipelined requests take 1.90 s against 0.78 s sequential.
findings.title: `toksec_pipeline_depth` is silently accepted-then-discarded, and pipelined requests each cost a 100 ms poll timeout

limitations: RCE verdict is none found within the audited scope; this build has no CGI, exec, or dynamic module path, so RCE requires memory corruption
Fuzzing bounds but cannot prove the absence of all memory-safety bugs
TLS was exercised end-to-end with a self-signed RSA-2048 certificate and crafted ClientHellos; client-certificate authentication and post-handshake (TLS 1.3) message paths were not covered

Memory measurements separate real growth from ASan allocator quarantine: the ASan build's RSS climb (27,636kB over 20,000 connections) is quarantine retention, not a leak, while the production build is flat at 0kB growth after warmup; load testing was single-host and not a distributed concurrency stress
Soak and memory probes were single-host; concurrent-worker races beyond 4 forked workers and distributed load were not stressed
RCE verdict is upstream-dependent: the proxy itself executes no code, so a code-executing backend route is what turns smuggling into RCE
Requires `proxy_pass` with a URI component; with a bare `proxy_pass http://up` (no URI) the raw target is forwarded and the decoded control characters are not used
Fuzzing bounds but cannot prove absence of all memory-safety bugs
Concurrent multi-host attack traffic beyond a single-host loopback harness was not exercised
Truncation is timing dependent in magnitude (127,860-2,097,152 of 2,097,152 observed) but the 16 KiB threshold truncated in 3/3 on every build tested

The query-smuggling RCE (SEC-003) needs an upstream that percent-decodes the request line and then splits it on whitespace/CRLF; a byte-exact upstream that never decodes sees one long token and does not split
Accepting POST would need body draining too; this build 405s every non-GET instead, so the desync is unconditional on any proxy location
Divergence needs the upstream to emit a bare LF in a header value; a fully CRLF-conforming upstream does not trigger it
The 100 ms figure is this build's poll timeout reproduced on loopback; slower paths add to it
Front-proxy amplification was reasoned from the socket behaviour, not measured through a real proxy
methods: Static source review of all 60 lines, including the 32 KiB streaming buffer arithmetic
256 single-byte percent-decode probe plus 100-16000 byte encodings
Event-loop lifecycle stress (partial requests, backpressure, churn, pipelining)
structured parser fuzzing: 3 seeds x 1000 plus 3 seeds x 2000 = 9000 iterations
raw binary fuzzing with random chunk splits: 3 seeds x 500 = 1500 iterations
proxy probe through a controlled Python upstream, plus 15 malformed-upstream modes
TLS ClientHello probe: 32 adversarial ALPN/SNI structural cases plus 400 crafted-handshake fuzz iterations under ASan
ASan+UBSan+_GLIBCXX_DEBUG build of the frozen release, all sanitizer logs empty

Sustained-load soak and allocator-aware memory probe: 4 forked workers under nginx_mw.conf, 5,000 sequential keep-alive requests against the production build with per-request fd sampling, plus 20,000 sequential keep-alive requests against the ASan build and 20,000 new connections against both the production and ASan builds to compare RSS growth
Live malicious-upstream smuggle test: controlled upstream echoing the parsed request head
Encoded-CRLF request-line injection, two forms (header injection and injected second request)
Trailing-byte truncation sweep: 0/1024/4090/4096/8192/16384/32768/65536 bytes written after the header terminator against a 2 MiB file, three trials per row, Connection: close
